subject: Clarify: short-burst metering and rounding treatment for webhook microrequests
messages:
From: Alex Hsu <alex.hsu@acme-retail.com>

Cc: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@acme-retail.com>

Subject: Metering question — many tiny webhook calls

Rachel —

Thanks again for the demo last week. One follow-up from our infra team: Acme has a pattern of many short webhook-driven requests that generate tiny payloads (typically ~40–120 tokens output; prompts ~20 tokens). In aggregate that's a lot of calls, but each call is very small. We want to understand how Redwood will meter those and what rounding/minimums we should expect so we can model monthly spend.

Two specific asks:
1) If we send 10k calls/day with average prompt+response = 150 tokens, how will that be billed? Do you round per-call to a minimum billing quantum?
2) If we enable conversation context reuse (prefix cache) for the same user across calls, does that reduce billed tokens or only affect latency?

We've attached a tiny spreadsheet with sample traffic if that helps.

Cheers,
Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Retail

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@acme-retail.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Metering question — many tiny webhook calls

Alex —

Thanks for the clear examples and the spreadsheet — helpful. Below is a concise walkthrough of how Redwood meters short-burst requests and how context/prefix caching interacts with billing. I included a numeric example tailored to your 10k/day case so you can drop the numbers into your model.

Summary answers first:
- Billing unit: we meter tokens consumed (prompt + generated tokens) with per-request rounding to our billing quantum (default 8-token quantum for hosted SKUs).
- Minimum per-request rounding applies independently to each request unless you use our persistent conversation session mode (see below).
- Prefix/KV cache reduces compute and latency but does not invisibly zero out billed prompt tokens — we offer amortized prefix credits when the same cached prefix is reused within a pinned session window.

Numeric example (your numbers):
- Average per call: 20 prompt tokens + 130 generated tokens = 150 total tokens.
- Billing quantum: 8 tokens. We round up to the nearest quantum per-call. 150 / 8 = 18.75 -> rounded to 19 quanta -> billed tokens = 19 * 8 = 152 tokens per call.
- Daily calls: 10,000 -> daily billed tokens = 10,000 * 152 = 1,520,000 tokens -> monthly (30 days) = 45,600,000 tokens.

Session mode + prefix amortization (optional, recommended for webhooks with stable prefixes):
- If you open a persistent session (session TTL 24h, pinned to user id), the runtime holds a cached prefix (e.g., persona/context) and we apply an amortized credit for repeated reuse of that prefix. The first call pays full prompt tokens; subsequent calls within the amortization horizon receive a credit equivalent to the prefix token count divided across N calls (configurable).
- Example: prefix = 40 tokens; amortization window splits that across first 100 calls in the session -> credit per call = 0.4 tokens (rounded later by quantum rules). In practice this reduces billed prompt tokens meaningfully for many small repeated calls.

Rounding caveats and recommended settings for Acme:
- Default hosting quantum is 8 tokens; for pilot customers we can evaluate moving you to a 4-token quantum to reduce rounding overhead on microcalls.
- Billing is per-request after rounding. Aggregation across calls (for credits) only happens if calls are under a single session id and you enable "session amortization" in the API call.

Next steps I suggest:
1) We run your spreadsheet through our costing tool (I can do this if you send a sample log or the anonymized traffic counts).
2) If rounding is a concern we can trial a 4-token quantum for your pilot month.
3) If you want to avoid per-call rounding entirely, we can discuss a reserved capacity commit where we offer a blended per-token rate + seat-style commit to absorb short-burst granularities.

I'll loop Markus here for any pricing flexibility/commit asks.

—Rachel

Alex / Rachel —

Quick internal note copied into thread so Alex sees it: pricing options that reduce rounding loss include (ranked by discount impact):
1) Short pilot commit (3 months, $X/month) — we can shrink quantum to 4 tokens and apply a 6% "rounding recovery" rebate applied monthly based on observed microcall distribution.
2) Reserved capacity pool — commit to a GPU pool and we give you a blended per-token price (no per-request rounding overhead on the pool side; you still see per-request rounding on hosted SKU but it's largely immaterial compared to the blended discount).
3) Hybrid seat+token — allocate seat bundles (100 seats) that give you N free small-call allowances per seat per day; good for very chatty user populations.

Operationally, for the amortized prefix credit we cap the amortization window at 10k calls or 24 hours (whichever comes first) to prevent abuse; we can set your default to 100-call amortization for user sessions. We also support an explicit header so you can signal "session-id" to maximize prefix reuse.

If Alex is ok, we can run a 30-day pilot with option 1 and produce an invoice credit to reconcile rounding for the pilot.

—Markus
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
